Screenshots in /tmp/qa/out and /tmp/qa/out-phone (scratch, not committed).

Changelog: `crates/app/changelog.json` 2026-11-05, id `vault-search`.

Not checked: the desktop build (web-only UI, but `cloud/` is on the qa-check skill's desktop list, so worth a look before release); a real signed-in account against the live project (the mock stands in for the server, so the read path itself is unchanged and untested here); iPhone 13 / WebKit.

evidence: VaultFilter in cloud/shared_builds.rs with matches and is_empty; seven tests in cloud::shared_builds::vault_filter_tests cover the unset filter, term conjunction, case, facet conjunction, visibility, tags and a blank query. Workspace nextest 355/355, lint:rust and fmt:rust:check clean.

VaultPanel draws the search form, four facet selects and the N-of-M count; facet_options builds the options from the rows. Two defects found by driving the app and fixed: duplicate option keys panicking Dioxus (a_facet_offers_each_id_once, which fails against the old sort-then-dedup_by with three rows and passes with two, so the fixture is the shape that matters) and blank selects on a restored filter (selected: on each option). an_unambiguous_name_is_not_qualified pins the archetype qualifier. Web Q/A: tank 125 of 1000, tank sonic 9 of 1000, Tanker 125, +Sonic Aura 6, +Private 0, no-match message, Clear filters 1000. Workspace nextest 355/355, lint:rust and fmt:rust:check clean.

BrowserState carries vault: VaultFilter and vault_sort: VaultSort, both serde-defaulted; the signals live in BrowserModal and VaultPanel mutates them through the modal's one save_state funnel. a_saved_state_round_trips_whole carries a populated vault filter and sort; missing_facets_restore_the_rest asserts a save without them opens unfiltered in the default order. In the app: Archetype -> Brute, close and reopen -> 141 of 1000 with the dropdown reading Brute; reload the page and reopen -> the same.

Both readings are the game, and one bit divides them: Granite's DDR template carries IgnoreStrength (flags_raw 0x430) and the seven Super Reflexes DDR templates do not (0x420; Evasion 0x60). The owner's screenshot of the game's own Defense Resistance breakdown on a level-50 Super Reflexes character (2026-11-05) — Evasion / Focused Fighting / Focused Senses +27.66%, Agile / Dodge / Lucky +13.58 / 13.66 / 13.62%, against the engine's unenhanced 17.30 and 8.65 — is the unflagged half; the flat Granite ladder is the flagged half. The reading came as that screenshot rather than the planned 0-vs-3-IO test-server run, and it settles the question outright because Agile, Dodge and Lucky are identical in the data (same Defense/All scale 0.2, same Melee_Res_Boolean table, same boosts_allowed of Buff_Defense alone) yet the game gives all three a different number, which only each power's own Defense enhancement can do.
apply.rs apply_debuff_resistance multiplies each routed row by 1 + enh.get(aspect), the aspect being the resisted attribute's own — debuff_resistance_enhancement_aspect maps defense/endurance/recharge/tohit/accuracy/range and returns None for perception, recovery, regeneration and the collapsed movement slot, which have no enhancement category and read unenhanced flagged or not; the same attrib-keyed rule apply_mez_resistance already uses. debuff_resistance_value now returns a DebuffResistance row carrying the atom's ignore_strength, because only at the reader is the granting atom still in hand. buff_pets::enh_multiplier already gated on ignoreStrength and now shares the same aspect map, so a slotted buff-pet and the power it copies agree. DDR-1's block comment is rewritten as DDR-2 and records that the beta's debuffResEnhMapping and Mids' GBPA_Pass1_EnhancePreED had the multiplier and not the flag, and that DDR-1 kept the wrong half of that verdict.
tests/debuff_resistance_not_enhanced.rs is renamed debuff_resistance_enhancement.rs; unfiled-3's granite_defense_ddr_ignores_defense_enhancement keeps its name and still passes. 9 tests: Granite flat 0..6 IOs on all four forks; Focused Fighting climbs by exactly the factor Granite's positional Smashing defense takes, measured rather than hardcoded; Consume's endurance row takes EnduranceReduction and not Defense; the Mastermind's Sonic Siphon recharge row takes Recharge and not Resistance/Accuracy/Range; Focused Senses' perception row stays put while its defense row climbs; the two ceiling tests unchanged. Broke it on purpose, both ways: drop the multiplier and five tests die, the_ignore_strength_flag_... first at 'Focused Fighting with 6 Defense IOs reads 17.30 against its unslotted 17.3'; ignore the flag and granite_defense_ddr_ignores_defense_enhancement dies at 'Granite moved off 43.25 with 6 Defense IOs: 73.48' — the number Mids and the beta produce and the game contradicts. nextest 360/360, lint:rust clean, fmt:rust:check clean, baseline:check holds every field on all four datasets.
In-app Q/A on the rebuilt web bundle (dx build --platform web, served on 8787) with a new fixture fixtures/qa/sr-ddr-probe.skif (level-50 Tanker, Super Reflexes / Super Strength, Focused Fighting 4 + Agile 1 + Dodge 2 + Lucky 3 level-50 Defense IOs): Detailed Totals ▸ Debuff Resistance reads Defense 65.57%, breakdown Focused Fighting +28.07%, Lucky +13.71%, Dodge +12.94%, Agile +10.85%, Total +65.57% — three data-identical powers reading three different numbers, as the game's breakdown does. fixtures/qa/granite-ddr-probe.skif still reads Defense 43.25% with Granite Armor +43.25% at six Defense IOs. Console clean. Not checked on phones or desktop: the change is engine math with no layout or target-conditional file touched.
Census for what this can actually move, four datasets' player sets: defense (39 powers), endurance (Consume, Psionic Shield) and recharge (the Mastermind's Sonic Siphon) are the only mapped types a build can fire — tohit has ten unflagged rows and none sits in a power accepting ToHit enhancement, and no unflagged accuracy or range row exists. Empathy's Fortitude, named in the finding, never reaches the caster's own totals at all (apply::is_ally_only skips ally-only buffs), and Sonic Siphon carries these self rows UNFLAGGED on the Mastermind's set and FLAGGED on the Defender's, Controller's and Corruptor's — the flag is per row, not per power name.

says: A VEAT build opened from Homecoming's Vault loses the display name and icon of every power that lives in a branch set.
body: Reported by a user 2026-11-05 about Homecoming's new Vault link: "issues loading in VEAT builds (will import, but it won't recognize the power names of several things so you end up with borked icons and internal names)". Not the same defect as unfiled-19 - that one spent power picks and shifted the by-level grid; this one leaves every pick where it belongs and breaks only the definition lookup. The client hands over one flat run of `Widow_Training.*` lines with the base set's and the branch's powers interleaved in purchase order, and `game_import::push` seated the primary list at whichever line arrived first and then dropped the `id` it was handed for every later pick, so picks from the other set were filed under that seat with `powerset: None`. `skif::hydrate` widens its NAME lookup across the archetype's branch sets (`Resolver::branch_powersets`), so the ident itself still resolves - even its case, which `client_build::title_case` had mangled from `NW_Slash` to `Nw_Slash` - but it keeps the seated set as the pick's own, and the app renders a power through `view::power_view::resolve_power_def`, an exact `find_power(powerset, ident)` with no widening. A base seat paired with a branch ident names nothing, and Rule 1's fallback is the report verbatim: the internal name beside the unknown icon. Only a VEAT can show this, because only a VEAT has picks whose real set differs from the seat - which is why the whole .mbd/.mxd//buildsave/Vault corpus read clean before the fix and after it. `crate::mbd_import`'s `push` has stamped the pick since the base-seat fix; the game reader is the one that lagged, and no fixture arrived with base and branch picks mixed, so the hole was ungraded on both game formats.

evidence: game_import.rs `push` now mirrors `mbd_import::push`: on an already-open selection it stamps `pick.powerset = Some(id)` whenever the pick's resolved set differs from the seat, and leaves it unstated when they agree, so an ordinary build still saves no redundant set on any pick. Both orders are covered by the seat's own behaviour: base-first stamps the branch picks, branch-first seats the branch and leans on `skif::seat_base_sets` to move the seat while every pick keeps the set it was stamped with. New crates/coh_data/tests/veat_branch_picks_keep_their_set.rs, four legs on one LEGAL Night Widow (one pick per level per column, each at or above its `available` level): the Vault client JSON, the same build as `/buildsave` text, the branch line first, and charnel.txt as the control that no ordinary pick states a set. Each VEAT leg grades the pair the UI actually uses - `find_power(pick.powerset, pick.internal_name)` - not just the ident, which is what let the old code pass while the user saw internal names. Broke it on purpose: dropping the stamp fails all three VEAT legs with `["arachnos-widow/widow-training :: NW_Mental_Blast", ..., "arachnos-widow/teamwork :: Elude"]` (10 picks) and leaves the control green. cargo nextest --workspace 364/364; lint:rust (clippy -D warnings) and fmt:rust:check clean; baseline:check holds every field of every build on all four forks. In-app Q/A on the rebuilt web bundle (dx build --platform web, serve.cjs on :8787, headless Chromium), driving the user's own step - navigating to `/#<fragment>` with a Vault-shaped link (raw deflate + base64url over the client's JSON, the fixtures/import-link/vault arm). BEFORE and AFTER run the SAME link, the legal Night Widow the test carries, each on a freshly cleaned bundle with a plain no-fragment load confirmed first. BEFORE, fix removed: the receipt reads "the linked build - 20 powers. Everything in the file resolved against this dataset" while the Powers panel reads L7 NW_Mental_Blast, L11 NW_Smoke_Grenade, L18 NW_Slash, L21 NW_Eviscerate, L23 NW_Psychic_Scream, L5 Pain_Tolerance, L19 NW_Mask_Presence, L23 NW_Mind_Link, L27 NW_Tactical_Training:_Vengeance, L29 Elude - ten internal names, and the screenshot shows the red question-mark placeholder on those rows while the base rows (Poison Dart, Strike, Dart Burst, Confront, Combat Training: Defensive, Tactical Training: Maneuvers, Indomitable Will, Foresight, Fly) show artwork. AFTER, fix in: the same ten rows read Mental Blast, Smoke Grenade, Slash, Eviscerate, Psychic Scream, Pain Tolerance, Mask Presence, Mind Link, Tactical Training: Vengeance, Elude, with zero internal names on screen and all 20 rows rendering real icons. Console errors none on both. (A check script that asks whether a display name APPEARS in the panel text is not a test: `NW_Slash` contains "Slash", so that measure read 2/8 on the broken build where the honest count is 0/8. The pass/fail reads the internal-name count.) The receipt's "Everything in the file resolved" line is unchanged and was false before - it reports the name lookups, which the branch widening already satisfied, not the (set, ident) pair the renderer needs; left alone here as out of scope and worth its own finding. Not checked in the app: the desktop and phone targets (the change is in coh_data, shared by every target, no layout touched) and Rebirth / Thunderspy / Brainstorm (Thunderspy ships Tarantula branch sets with the same TR_ shape and no VEAT fixture imports them from a game file; the stamp reads each fork's own `Archetype::branches`). Secondary finding, measured and NOT changed: `client_build::title_case` re-capitalises every underscore word, so it mangles 202 / 3484 Homecoming power idents (153 / 2841 rebirth, 175 / 2877 thunderspy, 202 / 3484 brainstorm) - `Hymn_of_Dissonance` to `Hymn_Of_Dissonance`, `EMP_Arrow` to `Emp_Arrow`, `X-Ray_Beam` to `X-ray_Beam`. Harmless today, because hydrate's case-insensitive pass repairs the ident and no mangled spelling collides with a real ident in the same set (0 collisions across all four forks), so `dataset_ident`'s display-name fallback is simply dead for those 202 powers. Changelog item veat-vault-import-names.

title: A summoned entity's full effect set reaches the planner
thesis: On every fork, a power that deals through a summoned entity shows that entity's foe −Damage-Resistance debuff in its effects and its damage in its damage — Acid Mortar reads −Resist 20% beside −Defense 20% and carries a Toxic damage row, on Homecoming, Rebirth, Brainstorm and Thunderspy alike.
body:
Asked 2026-11-05, as part of the report: "Some powers don't even show their full effects. Acid Mortar for example will not show its -res effect but will show the -def effect only if it is slotted for defense debuff enhancement."

Two separate defects sit under it, both found by measurement rather than read off the report:

1. The −Res row never reaches the contract on three of four forks. The foe-debuff route for Homecoming/Rebirth/Brainstorm is the name-keyed `DEBUFF_ATTRIBS` table, which has entries only for endurance/recovery/regeneration/tohit/base_defense; a `Resistance`-aspect row whose attribs are damage types matches nothing there, and `extractBuffAura` has already early-returned on its `scale > 0` gate. Thunderspy's branch keys on the TABLE token instead (`res_dmg` in `_TSPY_DEBUFF_SIGNED`) and emits `ResistanceDebuff`. Measured over the generated pet-entities: abilities with a negative-scale `*_Res_Dmg` atom and no emitted effect number 31 / 35 / 31 (HC / RB / BNS) against 1 (TSPY, which keeps 34).

2. The entity's damage is skipped outright. `damage.rs::follows_owner` reads `canZone` as "a kept pet", and `resolve_summoned` drops such an entity's rows, so Acid Mortar projects zero damage components. 22 distinct player powers summon a damage-dealing, non-commandable, `canZone: true` entity.

## Decisions

Decided 2026-11-05, user: the `resolve_summoned` skip is a bug to fix, not a modelling choice to keep.

Decided 2026-11-05, agent, not objected to: the fix goes in the CONVERTER, not the engine. `pseudo_pet_effects` merges what the entity's summarized `effects` array carries; teaching the engine to read `atoms` instead would give the entity's rows two independent routes into the projection and a second precedence to keep in step. The Thunderspy rule already exists and already works, so the other three forks gain a rule rather than inventing one.

## Preconditions

- Checked 2026-11-05: the Thunderspy rule fires — Acid Mortar projects `resistanceDebuff=20.00 defenseDebuff=20.00` there and `defenseDebuff=20.00` alone on the other three.
- Checked 2026-11-05: the −Res templates are byte-comparable across forks (`Ranged_Res_Dmg`, scale −2.0, `flags: ["IgnoreStrength"]`, attribs = the eight damage types), so the table token exists in the Homecoming source the same way it does in Thunderspy's.
- `npm run regen` is the only writer of `pipeline/`; the contract bundles are built from it.

## Out of scope

- The report's second half — "will show the -def effect only if it is slotted for defense debuff enhancement" — does NOT reproduce. The −Defense row is present at every level from 1 to 50 and in every archetype that holds the power, slotted or not (base 20.00, Defender 26.60), and a slotted L50 Defense Debuff IO moves it to 28.476. Nothing here fixes it because nothing is wrong with it; it needs the reporter's own build to chase.
- How a routed −Res row is ENHANCED. That is the existing debuff-resistance rule (worklog unfiled-5) and is unchanged here; this plan is only about the row existing.
- Pets that are themselves the character (a Mastermind's commanded pets) — `summoned_entity_chain` already declines a commandable root, and this plan does not touch that.

says: The converter classifies a foe −Damage-Resistance row on Homecoming, Rebirth and Brainstorm, not only on Thunderspy
body:
The row is authored as the eight damage-type attribs at aspect=Resistance with a negative scale on a `*_Res_Dmg` table. The ASPECT is what makes it a resistance rather than damage, so no name-keyed table can hold it: DEBUFF_ATTRIBS keys position and resource attribs and deliberately holds no damage-type key, extractBuffAura declines it on its `scale > 0` gate, extractDamageStrength on its aspect=Strength gate. It reached the last branch it could reach and there was none.

Thunderspy has had the rule since ENT-4, inline in its own branch. It is now a shared predicate both branches call, so the forks cannot drift apart again. `Heal_Dmg` is excluded — at aspect=Resistance it is heal-debuff resistance, the same reading that gates the heal emitters either side of it — and a `*_Ones` table is a marker, not a percent, so it stays dropped.

says: A summoned entity that is the power's payload folds its damage; a companion still does not
body:
`follows_owner` read `canZone` as "a kept pet", and the villain defs set that flag on things that never move — Acid Mortar is a mortar that sits where it was placed — so the guard dropped the payload with the companion and the power read as a non-attack.

`canZone` stays the entry to the question; the answer is what the entity does. One damaging ability (a payload, not a rotation), or `oneShot` (it detonates and never has a rotation to build), or a window at or past PERMANENT_LIFESPAN (already read as ONE activation, so folding it cannot produce a lifetime total) — anything else is a creature running a rotation for as long as it lives.

title: A drag preview never promises a size the release refuses
thesis: Dragging a content-fitted panel's resize handle leaves the floating copy at the height the panel actually lands at — on Powers the copy reads 820px through every drag, where it read 980px against a committed 820px before this.
body:
Asked 2026-11-05, as its own report: "panels can't be resized to certain sizes even though the HUD suggests it can".

Two components draw a live drag and only one of them asked the grid what it would allow. `DragPlaceholder` resolves the pointer's box to a cell span and passes it through `clamp_resize` / `clamp_resize_height` / `clamp_resize_from_left` — the same functions the commit uses — so the ghost has always shown where the surface will land. `DragLayer`, the floating copy of the surface itself, drew `resize_box_px` raw. For a panel whose height is answered by its content, `clamp_resize_height` refuses any change at all, so the copy stretched down the page while the ghost and the committed box both stayed put: the preview promised a size the panel springs back from the moment the pointer leaves it, which is exactly what reads as the panel refusing to resize.

Measured on the built app before the fix, Powers (content-fitted) dragged +120,+160: copy 1035x980, ghost 1047x820, committed 1047x820.

says: The floating copy is held inside the bounds the release will clamp to, by the same functions the release calls
body: `clamped_resize_box_px` asks `clamp_resize`/`clamp_resize_height`/`clamp_resize_from_left` for the floor and the ceiling — the two asks being 0 and u32::MAX, so the clamp itself is never restated here — converts them to pixels and holds the pointer's box between them. Only the axis the clamp binds is held; the other keeps tracking the pointer unsnapped, so the copy still reads as stretching in place rather than snapping to cells. On a west drag a width the clamp pulled back moves the left edge with it, because the right edge is that gesture's anchor.

says: On screen, a fitted panel's copy never outgrows its committed box, and an unfitted panel still resizes in height
done_when: A person drags the Powers panel's resize handle down and right and sees the floating copy the same height as the dashed outline and as the panel it becomes; then drags the Info panel's handle down and sees it grow.
body: The complaint was about what the HUD suggests, so the check is on screen. Powers is content-fitted and must hold its height through the drag; Info is not and must not, which is the half that would break if the clamp bound where it should not.

evidence: `clamped_resize_box_px` in crates/app/src/grid/view.rs takes the floor and ceiling from `clamp_resize(&item, 0, 0)` and `clamp_resize(&item, u32::MAX, u32::MAX)` — and from `clamp_resize_from_left` at the two asks that bracket a west drag's room — converts them to pixels and holds the pointer's box between them, so no second copy of the sizing rules lives in the view. `DragLayer`'s resize arm calls it; `DragPlaceholder` was already calling the same three functions, so preview, ghost and commit now share one answer.

Built the debug web bundle and drove it with Playwright at 1600x1200 on fixtures/buildsave/homecoming/charnel.txt, measuring the floating copy, the dashed ghost and the committed surface mid-drag and after release. Powers (content-fitted): drag(120,160) copy 1035x820 ghost 1047x820 committed 1047x820; drag(60,400) copy 1107x820 ghost 1047x820 committed 1047x820; drag(-120,200) copy 927x820 ghost 915x820 committed 915x820 — the copy's height is 820 in every one, where the same drag(120,160) read copy 1035x980 against a committed 1047x820 before the fix. Info (not fitted) still follows the pointer: drag(0,160) copy 256x1086 committed 256x1072, drag(0,-160) copy 256x912 committed 256x928, so the clamp binds only where the commit binds. Console clean. One gap this does NOT close, and did not open: on a fitted panel a width change re-measures the content, so widening Available 3->4 columns left the ghost at 784px while the panel settled at 460px — the ghost cannot know a height the content has not been measured at yet. Screenshots in target/qa/.

title: Re-plan when a power is taken by dragging it
thesis: A power in the by-level grid can be dragged to a different pick and everything between the two slides along one pick, so a build can be re-planned without un-picking and re-slotting the powers below the change.
body:
Requested 2026-11-10, owner (in conversation, with a screenshot of a Stone Armor / Water Blast build): move Speed of Sound from level 47 back to level 18 and have everything from 18 onward move forward one pick, instead of unselecting and re-slotting every power from 18 to 49.

Decided 2026-11-10, owner (in conversation):
- ONE gesture. Dropping a power on another level shifts every power between the two one pick along, in BOTH directions. Dragging forwards is allowed where every carried power still meets its own unlock level, and refused with the reason when not.
- The old drag-and-swap goes away. It traded the two ends and left the ladder between them untouched, which is the shape of the problem the request is about.
- The owner expected forwards drags to need a pile of checks and to be a step too far. They are not: the per-power unlock-floor test the press already runs for every cell answers it over the range instead, so both directions cost one loop.
- A drop that crosses no power (onto an empty pick) is the plain move to that level it looks like, because an empty cell carries nothing.

What stays:
- Only the stored level changes, so slots, enhancements and toggles travel with the power and the slot-level solver re-houses any slot the new level can no longer serve.
- The picker's own rules still bind, applied to every carried pick rather than only the dragged one: each lands at or above its floor, level 1 keeps one primary and one secondary, and Level Up mode refuses anything above the character.
- The existing out-of-order mark still reports a build whose prerequisites are now taken too late; the shift does not try to prevent that, it only prevents levels the game would not grant.

Out of scope:
- Reordering within a powerset rather than by level: the by-powerset layout has no level ladder to move along.
- Choosing a level by typing it: the drag is the affordance the request asked for.

says: Dropping a pick on another cell shifts every pick between the two one cell along, in both directions, instead of trading the two ends' levels.
done_when: A drop that crosses powers moves the dragged pick to the target's level and every pick between the two to the next pick along, so nothing collides and no cell is left holding two picks; a drop onto an empty cell moves only the dragged pick.

An empty cell is carried by position and holds no pick, so a drop crossing no power is the plain move-to-that-level it looks like. Only the stored level is written, so slots, enhancements and toggles travel with the power. Nine unit tests in the module's own test mod; three of them die when shift_sources is broken from remove/insert to swap (a_shift_reorders_the_cells_and_leaves_none_behind, dropping_a_late_power_on_an_early_one_pushes_the_run_down_one_pick, level_one_keeps_one_primary_and_one_secondary), which was checked by making that change and reverting it. Workspace suite 372/372; lint:rust and fmt:rust:check clean. In the built web app at 1700x1100 on fixtures/buildsave/homecoming/sisterachlys.txt, dragging Tactics from L49 onto the L18 cell read status "Move to level 18, and 12 powers to their next pick" and landed Tactics at L18 with Chain Lightning, Kuji-In Toh, Cloudburst, Kick, Category Five, Tough, Golden Dragonfly, Weave, Acrobatics, Spring Attack, Snow Storm and Frozen Armor each one pick later, Maneuvers at L49, and every card's enhancement chips still populated with their levels (Tactics keeping its own 18).

crates/app/src/panels/powers_by_level.rs: shift_refusal replaces move_refusal and decides the drop over every pick the shift carries, not just the dragged one. Three terms, in the picker's own words: each arriving pick lands at or above its own unlock floor (pick_floor, which raises a power's unlock level to its set's pool/epic floor); Level Up mode refuses any carried pick above the character's level; and a trial shift then counts level-1 picks per bucket, because a VEAT branch pick sits in a role list under its own set id. A pick whose def does not resolve makes the whole drag uncarriable rather than silently skipping it. The per-cell verdict is still fixed once at the press. Four tests pin the terms (a_shift_that_would_pull_a_carried_power_below_its_floor_is_refused, an_unresolvable_pick_cannot_be_carried, level_up_mode_refuses_a_carried_pick_above_the_character, level_one_keeps_one_primary_and_one_secondary). In the built web app on sisterachlys.txt, mid-drag the DOM read 14 pick-cell--target, 8 pick-cell--refused, 1 source and 1 hovered target; hovering the L1 cell with Tactics showed "Tactics unlocks at level 14, so it can't be taken at 1", the cell wore pick-cell--refused, and releasing left Tactics at L49.

title: Re-plan when a power is taken by dragging it
thesis: In the by-level grid, dropping a power on another card's middle third swaps their two levels while dropping on its top or bottom edge inserts before or after that power and slides everything in between one pick along.
satisfied_when: level-order-shift-1, level-order-shift-2 and level-order-shift-3 all ticked
body:
Requested 2026-11-10, owner (in conversation, with a screenshot of a Stone Armor / Water Blast build): move Speed of Sound from level 47 back to level 18 and have everything from 18 onward move forward one pick, instead of unselecting and re-slotting every power from 18 to 49 — while keeping the ability to swap two powers' levels directly.

Decided 2026-11-10, owner (in conversation):
- TWO drop zones on each card (CellBand): the middle third swaps the two powers' levels (or moves into an unspent pick without touching anything else), and the top and bottom thirds insert before or after that power, sliding every pick in between one cell along.
- Why bands of the card rather than only the gap between cards: measured in the built app at 1700x1100, cards are 57px tall and `.power-column` puts a 3px gap between them. A 3px sliver cannot be aimed at reliably with a mouse and is unusable on touch, so the top and bottom 19px thirds stand in for the seam — and the 3px gap itself also snaps to that seam so crossing between two stacked cards never drops hover.
- Both sides of a seam (`After` cell k and `Before` cell k+1) resolve via `insert_target` to the same destination in both directions, and draw a 2px insertion bar in that exact 3px seam (`::before` / `::after`).
- Both directions (backwards and forwards) are supported: `drop_refusal` checks every pick touched by the chosen operation.

What stays:
- Only the stored level changes, so slots, enhancements and toggles travel with the power and the slot-level solver re-houses any slot the new level can no longer serve.
- The picker's own rules bind on every moved pick: each lands at or above its floor, level 1 keeps one primary and one secondary, and Level Up mode refuses anything above the character.
- The existing out-of-order mark still reports a build whose prerequisites are now taken too late.

Out of scope:
- Reordering within a powerset rather than by level: the by-powerset layout has no level ladder to move along.
- Choosing a level by typing it: the drag is the affordance the request asked for.

says: Dropping on a card's middle third swaps the two levels (or moves onto an unspent pick), while dropping on its top or bottom third (or the 3px gap between stacked cards) inserts before or after that power with a seam indicator.
done_when: In the built web app, hovering a card's middle outlines the card and swaps only the two powers on release, while hovering the top edge, bottom edge of the card above, or the 3px gap between them lights the seam between them and inserts there, shifting only the powers in between.

evidence: crates/app/src/panels/powers_by_level.rs and crates/app/assets/app.css: CellBand divides each 57px card into Before (top third), Middle (middle third) and After (bottom third), and PickDrag::band_at also claims the 3px vertical gap between stacked cards in the same column so crossing a seam never flickers hover to None. Middle resolves to DropMode::Swap (apply_swap trades the two powers' levels, or moves only the dragged pick onto an unspent cell); Before and After resolve via insert_target(from, slot) to DropMode::Insert so After cell k and Before cell k+1 agree in both drag directions. CSS draws a dashed outline + fill for pick-cell--swap and a 2px bar in the 3px seam via pick-cell--insert-before::before / pick-cell--insert-after::after, suppressed when the band's verdict is refused. 14 unit tests pass in panels::powers_by_level::tests (including a_swap_trades_only_the_two_levels, a_middle_drop_onto_an_unspent_pick_moves_only_the_dragged_power, a_swap_is_refused_when_the_occupant_cannot_descend, the_middle_of_a_card_swaps_and_the_edges_insert_before_or_after, swap_and_insert_disagree_about_who_moves). Verified in the built web app on sisterachlys.txt: L16 bottom edge (pick-cell--insert-after), the 3px gap L16..L18 (pick-cell--insert-before) and L18 top edge (pick-cell--insert-before) all read "Insert at level 18, and 12 powers to their next pick"; L18 middle (pick-cell--swap) read "Swap levels with Chain Lightning" and committed Tactics L49<->Chain Lightning L18 with nothing between moved; then dragging Maneuvers L47 to L16's bottom edge committed Maneuvers->L18 and shifted the 11 powers in L18..L44 one pick later while leaving Chain Lightning at L49.

title: The inherent panels remember their fold
thesis: Each inherent panel's open-or-folded state survives a reload, while the groups inside the Powers panel still reset.
body:
Requested by the owner 2026-11-10: I sometimes slot inherents, but have to open them every time I open Sidekick. The fold in question is PowerGroup's inner fold, whose module note called it deliberately unpersisted when the groups were a section of the Powers panel; since inherent-panels (merged 2026-11-05) the panel's position, hidden set and pinned pill all persist, so the fold was the one property of the panel that did not survive.

Decided: the five inherent panels take a caller-owned fold signal, persisted as one preference under sk-inherent-folds and seeded with the authored defaults (Basic and Prestige folded, the rest open) so a fresh profile is unchanged. The groups inside the Powers panel and the by-level columns keep the session-local fold: those groups are the panel's own arrangement, not surfaces the user placed.

Out: persisting the Powers panel's group folds; a global expand-all control.

says: The five inherent panels read and write a persisted fold preference instead of a session-local one.
body: A new store beside hidden_inherents_store: one JSON object mapping the five InherentCategory values to open-or-folded, loaded at the shell root with the restored-gate pattern, seeded with the authored defaults so a fresh profile opens Basic and Prestige folded and the rest open. PowerGroup takes an optional caller-owned fold signal; only the inherent panels pass it. The Powers panel's groups and the by-level columns keep their session-local fold.

says: The remembered fold is verified in the running app: a fold survives a reload, and the Powers panel's groups still reset.
done_when: The owner reloads the app after folding an inherent panel and finds it still folded, then folds a group inside the Powers panel, reloads, and finds it open again.

evidence: crates/app/src/inherent_fold_store.rs: the store (sk-inherent-folds, one JSON object keyed by the lowercase InherentCategory names), default_folded carrying the authored defaults out of inherents_section, folded() reading stored-over-default, and the InherentFold handle PowerGroup takes. shell.rs provides the map at the root with the restored-gate pattern and persists it through storage::commit. power_group.rs takes an optional caller-owned fold that replaces the session-local signal; only inherents_section passes it, so the Powers panel groups and the by-level columns keep the session fold. group_starts_collapsed is gone — the defaults live in the store alone. InherentCategory gained PartialOrd/Ord for the BTreeMap key; InherentFold derives PartialEq for the component macro. title: The picker orders its IO sets by rarity
thesis: In the enhancement picker's IO Sets list the sort control offers rarity beside name and level, at either end of the ladder, and each rarity draws as one named, counted block whose sets run in level order.
body:
Reported by a user 2026-11-10: the enhancement picker's IO Sets list sorts by name or by
level, and looking through the larger unfiltered list they wanted rarity as a third order,
with each run of rarities sub-ordered by level. Rarity was already a filter; it was never an
order.

Decisions (2026-11-10, user-chosen when asked):
- BOTH directions, as two entries in the existing sort dropdown — "By rarity, common first"
  and "By rarity, rare first". The user asked for the choice outright. One entry could only
  pick a side, and the ladder has two obvious reading ends. Name and level keep one entry
  each: they have an obvious first row.
- The ladder is uncommon, rare, purple (Very Rare), then event, pvp, ato. The game's three
  rarity rungs first, in the order an item tooltip states them; the three tiers that name how
  a set is ACQUIRED after them, in the order the beta's own "all sets" view files them
  (`specialSortOrder` in EnhancementPicker.tsx: standard, purple, pvp, ato).
- Inside a chunk the order is the Level order — min level up, then name — in BOTH directions.
  A chunk is a run of levels whichever rarity is on top, so flipping the ladder flips the
  chunks and nothing else. Rejected: reversing the whole list for "rare first", which makes
  each chunk read backwards.
- Each chunk is headed with its label and its size, "Rare (4)", on the row that opens it.
  A single chunk gets no heading at all: filtered to one rarity, the heading would repeat the
  dropdown one line above it, on the same reasoning that leaves a one-option dropdown undrawn.
- A rarity token this build does not know is UNRANKED and keeps the last seat in either
  direction. It is not the rarest thing in the catalogue, and a fork's own vocabulary must not
  be filed there on a guess.

## Preconditions, checked 2026-11-10

- `SetSort` is one enum read by both the option list and its `onchange`, so a third order is
  one variant and one arm of one match; `picker_sets::offered_sets` is already the whole order.
- `rarity_label` already turns the export's `category` tokens into display names, so the
  heading reuses the filter's own vocabulary rather than inventing a second one.

## Out of scope

- Remembering the chosen sort between picker opens. The sort is component state today, like
  the sort of every other list in the picker; `picker_memory` remembers the FACETS, not order.
- Rarity ordering anywhere else. The Generic, Special and Origin tabs list enhancements, not
  sets, and have no sort control at all.
- A rarity order for the shopping list (`enhancement_list.rs`), which groups by what you buy.

says: the IO Sets sort offers By rarity, common first and By rarity, rare first; each rarity draws as one named, counted block and its sets run in level order inside it

evidence:
Landed 2026-11-10. `picker_sets::SetSort` gains RarityCommonFirst and RarityRareFirst plus
token/from_token, so the dropdown's option list and its onchange cannot disagree; the ladder is
`rarity_rank` (uncommon 0, rare 1, purple 2, event 3, pvp 4, ato 5, everything else
RARITY_UNRANKED) compared through `rarity_order`, which puts an unranked tier last in BOTH
directions. `chunk_headers` marks the row that opens each run and returns the run's size.
powers.rs draws one `.picker-set-entry` per set — the wrapper carries the key, because Dioxus
0.7 allows a key only on the FIRST node of a block and warns that it dropped the one on the
second — with `.picker-set-chunk` above the set. app.css styles both.

Broke it on purpose, seven ways, each dying in at least one test: swapping purple and event on
the ladder kills the ladder test and the header test; dropping the level sub-sort kills
each_rarity_chunk_reads_in_level_order; never drawing headers kills
a_header_names_each_rarity_run_with_its_size; dropping the single-chunk rule kills
one_rarity_gets_no_header; counting the rest of the list instead of the run kills the same
header test; treating an unknown rarity as the rarest kills

title: A two-click phase power shows its whole cycle on the card
thesis: On Homecoming, a power whose redirect table pairs two phases of one self-chained activation cycle (Temporal Bomb: place/attach, then detonate) projects its detonation payload and its real cycle costs on the Info card — damage components, Knockback, the Temporal Bubble buff/debuff rows, recharge 150s, cast 2.77s, endurance 26 — instead of the near-empty place-phase record, while every other redirect table in the corpus (the Kheldian form pairs included) ships unchanged.
body:
The report (2026-11-10): comparing Time Bomb (Rebirth/Thunderspy) with Temporal Bomb (Homecoming), the Temp card lacks damage and recharge, and its buff/debuff numbers show in Totals but not on the card.

Root cause, measured 2026-11-10: Homecoming reworked Time Bomb into a two-click phase power. The player record (Time_Bomb) carries no effects; four redirect branches pair kRemoteBomb Source.Mode? / its negation (place on a foe in melee / place at feet vs detonate) plus a never-firing Remote_Bomb_Info display record. The converter emitted the three selectable branches as formVariants, so the engine\u2019s first-match walk (ASFORM-1) swaps the whole record to the PLACE phase: the projection resolves accuracy, 2.77s cast and 26 endurance from the variant\u2019s stats and nothing else — zero damage components, zero effect rows. The payload was never lost: the base record\u2019s 27 union atoms already carry the detonation damage (traps 1.182 Fire / 0.818 Lethal on Melee_Damage; blaster 2.0 / 3.0), the Knockback and the Temporal Bubble rows (allies +37.5% run/fly/recharge/recovery, foes -50% run/fly, -40% recharge, -30% recovery for 30s), each with its own branch gate. Only the swap hid them, and no branch states the recharge — the 150s lives on the detonate branch\u2019s stats.

Fix shape decided 2026-11-10, agent, user picked the display (question: what should the fixed card show; answer: the detonation view — one card, damage/knockback/bubble/costs, not a split by phase). The converter declines the phase table for formVariants and stamps the base record\u2019s stats with the executing branches\u2019 union (accuracy, endurance, castTime from the place branches; recharge from the detonate branch; the never-fires Info branch excluded; two branches stating one field differently fails the regen loudly). The engine is unchanged: with no formVariants the base record projects whole, which is exactly the detonation view.

Preconditions, checked 2026-11-10:
- Engine probe on the shipped Homecoming bundle: Temporal Bomb (controller, L50) projects recharge None, cast 2.77, end 26, 0 damage components, 3 granted rows (stat tiles only). Rebirth Time Bomb on the same probe resolves whole (recharge 360, 2 damage components, 7 granted rows) — the defect is Homecoming/Brainstorm\u2019s form-variant swap, not the projection.
- Fix-shape probe on a patched bundle (formVariants removed on the 4 Time Bomb powers, stats stamped accuracy 2 / endurance 26 / castTime 2.77 / recharge 150): controller projects 61.2 damage (36.2 Fire + 25.0 Lethal), Knockback 8.31, Slow 50, -40% recharge, -30% recovery, +37.5% recharge, +37.5% recovery, buffDuration 30; blaster projects 278.1 damage (111.2 Fire + 166.8 Lethal) and Knockback. Numbers match the beta\u2019s measured ones.
- Corpus sweep of complementary single-mode redirect pairs (kX Source.Mode? beside its negation): exactly 16 tables — 8 Time Bomb family (Homecoming + Brainstorm x 4 archetypes) and 8 Kheldian form pairs (Gleaming Bolt, Glinting Eye, Shadow Bolt, Ebon Eye x 2 forks). The Kheldian records publish no Set_Mode and grant nothing — their modes are the shapeshift forms\u2019 — so the discriminator (the paired mode is published via Set_Mode by a power this power\u2019s own Grant_Power grants; the marker Temporary_Powers.Temporary_Powers.Time_Bomb carries Set_Mode RemoteBomb) selects the 8 Time Bomb tables and nothing else.
- Beta prior art (coh-sidekick-beta homecoming-parser-22, ticked 2026-10-16): the beta resolved the same family\u2019s payload by following the *_Info display powers; measured numbers agree (blaster 2.0/3.0 + KB 4, traps 1.182/0.818). The next converter\u2019s union path needs no Info-following: the payload already sits on the base record.
- npm run regen is deterministic and the only writer of pipeline/ (its own header); the regen-diff guard will show exactly what moved.

Out of scope:
- The two ally +37.5% Run/Fly rows are gated on the target\u2019s DisallowSpeedBoost token and are dropped by the display bag like every gate-carrying atom corpus-wide; changing that display policy is its own plan. The probe says the other six bubble rows resolve.
- The place-to-detonate grant walk (grantEdges for the bomb marker): the chain window does not model two-click sequences; nothing here changes that.
- Rebirth and Thunderspy Time Bomb: already whole, pinned only as a regression guard.
- What the perma tracker does once recharge 150 exists (30s bubble vs 150s recharge is not perma; the eligibility gate decides as for any power).
- Mids parity beyond the numbers measured; the in-game spot-check the beta flagged (traps 1.182/0.818 come from the generic Remote_Bomb_Info display record) carries over unchanged.

says: The converter recognises a two-click phase table (complementary kX Mode? pair whose mode a power this power grants publishes via Set_Mode), declines it for formVariants, and stamps the base record with the executing branches union stats.
Regenerated Homecoming and Brainstorm; the diff moves exactly the 8 Time Bomb powers (formVariants dropped, stats stamped) and nothing else; the Kheldian form pairs keep their formVariants.

Engine pins: on Homecoming the Temporal Bomb projection carries the detonation damage, Knockback, the six bubble rows, recharge 150 / cast 2.77 / end 26 on controller and blaster; Rebirth Time Bomb and Energy Transfer are unchanged.

A person opens a Homecoming build holding Temporal Bomb, pins it in the Info panel, and finds the Damage block (61.2 on a L50 controller), the Effects rows (Knockback, Slow -50%, -40% Recharge, -30% Recovery, +37.5% Recharge, +37.5% Recovery), Recharge 150s, Cast 2.77s, End 26.
done_when: The owner runs the rebuilt app on the HC dataset, opens the Temporal Bomb card, and confirms the detonation numbers are on it; the owner also records what the two target-token-gated +37.5% Run/Fly rows do (absent or noted).

One plan correction: Remote_Bomb_Target (attach-to-foe) also states range 7, so the attach reach stays in the union; the plan body had said only the never-fires Info record stated it. The Info record is still excluded, on principle (a record that never fires pays nothing); its stats are a subset of the union either way. Corpus guards: a mixed table (one claimed pair, one unattributed) warns and declines rather than half-claiming; two branches stating one stat differently throw the regen. The verify moved to file: terms because the worklog resolver collects .js but not .cjs sources, so fn: terms can never resolve against scripts/convert-powerset.cjs — a tool limitation, not a missing definition. clippy/fmt/eslint clean.

Regenerated homecoming and brainstorm with a temporary driver (deleted after) because npm run regen is blocked on this machine before conversion — recorded as unfiled-101 (prov8 Brainstorm client drift + the pre-existing build_io.rs:1340 partial roster). The regen moved exactly the 8 Time Bomb powers (4 per fork: traps controller/corruptor/defender + blaster/devices): formVariants dropped, stats stamped accuracy 2 / range 7 / endurance 26 / castTime 2.77 / recharge 150 (traps) and 360 (blaster). git diff --stat contract: 40 insertions, 14476 deletions across the 8 power records plus the two forks bundles; rebirth and thunderspy byte-identical; the coverage-census (structural zeros subset of baseline), atom-coverage (963/4958 shapes) and every other audit gate passed unchanged. The Kheldian form pairs were never formVariants — extractModeVariants claims them — so the regression pin is modeVariants presence on Gleaming Bolt, in phase_cycle_powers.rs::the_form_detectors_still_serve_their_tables. dsh8 worklist ended on brainstorm, matching the committed copy.

crates/coh_math/tests/phase_cycle_powers.rs, 5 tests, all green: the_temporal_bomb_card_is_the_detonation (HC controller L50: def ships no formVariants, stats stamped, recharge 150 / cast 2.77 / end 26, damage 61.17 = Fire 36.15 + Lethal 25.02, rows Knockback 8.31 / Slow 50 / -40% recharge / -30% recovery / +37.5% recharge / +37.5% recovery / duration 30s), the_blaster_bomb_is_its_own_record (Remote Bomb: recharge 360, 278.06 = Fire 111.22 + Lethal 166.84), brainstorm_ships_the_same_cycle, rebirth_time_bomb_is_unchanged (360 / 9s / 26 / 278.05 — the old numbers exactly), the_form_detectors_still_serve_their_tables (Energy Transfer keeps formVariants, Gleaming Bolt keeps modeVariants). The totals baselines moved only because the bundle hash moved: the COH_WRITE_BASELINE re-record shows the recorded answers byte-identical (diff is the bundleFnv1a64 stamp and byte count only, and the per-build sweep printed zero CHANGED builds on both forks). text: 2026-11-11: blocker 2 (audit-dataset-roster) is fixed — the vault-link test at build_io.rs:1340 now matches exhaustively over the four variants instead of a `_` arm, the gate passes, and the change is committed. Blocker 1 (prov8 Brainstorm drift) stands and is unfiled-100's to resolve: the re-export. Scoped the same day: the exporter reads the patched client cleanly; the patch removed ~92 powers (the Electrical Control rework — Jolting Chain and Synaptic Overload are gone from the new shard, tesla_cage remains) and carries a patch-wide chain_delay/ppm_mod field pair whose authored values (Trip Mine 2.8, Sonic Boom 3.25) land exactly where the parser documents them.

2026-11-11 (continued, same session as the roster-gate fix): the prov8 gate is diagnosed as a parser mislabeling of the field-41b block on the Nov 3 beta client, not stale hashes. The parser reads the block as [override, ppm_mod, chain_delay] — its docstring says the override is 0 = compute-from-geometry and PPMMod is 1.0 everywhere but the Sonic Aura pet's 2.0. The committed BS export (Sept 28 shards) matches: override on 6 powers (Trip Mine 2.8 x4, Hypnotizing Lights 1.0 x2), ppm_mod on 1 (pets/sonic_aura/sonic_boom = 2.0), chain_delay on ~60 (real chain powers 0.1-0.7). The scratch re-export from the Nov 3 client reads the same three words as: override ABSENT everywhere, ppm_mod = {0.0 x14955, 2.8 x6, 3.25 x5}, chain_delay = {1.0 x14967, 2.0 x1} — the override and PPMMod values landed in the OTHER two labels, and the real chain delays (0.3/0.5) appear nowhere. The exporter writes ppm_mod only when != 1.0 and chain_delay only when truthy, which hides none of this. A raw-byte census of an anchored record (ArchetypeX Sonic_Aura Sonic_Boom, record 3999) shows the words after arc are [3.25, 1.0, 0.0...] — the override and PPMMod values are where the parser's model says they are, so the parser's read is landing one f4 earlier than it should be. The parse is NOT globally shifted: the diff between committed and scratch exports is sane for ~14,960 powers (only ~200 have real effects churn), so the block is one f4 wide but the parser's read is misaligned by one f4 within the block, not the whole record. Attempted verification: a hand-walked field probe (fields 1-33, then raw words after arc) hit a record-boundary error, so the probe's field walk miscounted somewhere before 31 — the probe file exists at /tmp/opencode/raw_probe.py but needs correction before rerun. It is a diagnostic tool, not deliverable work. Next step for the fix: correct the probe's field walk to match the parser's field order exactly (fields 10-21 are 12 strings, 26-31 are 6 string_arrays), then verify the raw-byte census against the .powers oracle values (Chain_Lightning 0.3, Tesla_Cage 0.5) and decide whether the parser needs a new layout variant detected via _detect_format or the has_field_41b read order needs to change.

2026-11-11 (correction to the note above, measured on the re-export): the ~92 powers this item reported removed by the Electrical Control rework were never removed. Jolting Chain and Synaptic Overload are both present in the 2026-11-03 beta bin, in five set copies each. The ~92 was the parser failing on the 89 records that carry a chain delay - the field-41 misread below - added to the removals that are real. The real removals are 30 pet `avoid.json` files and the `sonic_thrust` and `strident_echo` redirects; git pairs one avoid file with a new `temporary_powers/poison.json` at 62% similarity and reports that as a rename, and the two files are unrelated. Committed tally for the fork: 6 added, 31 deleted, 1 renamed, 348 modified. The misread itself is unfiled-102.

2026-11-11: the roster fix that closed blocker 2 left its own file failing `npm run fmt:rust:check`. rustfmt wants the exhaustive match it added at crates/app/src/build_io.rs:1342 folded to `DatasetId::Rebirth | DatasetId::Thunderspy | DatasetId::Brainstorm => { OpenRoute::MoveTo(DatasetId::Homecoming) }`. Verified pre-existing at 4bcb72236 and untouched by the re-export commits, which change no `.rs` file at all; it is one `cargo fmt -p app` away from fixed.

evidence: Both blockers are gone on `prov8-beta-client-layout`. `node scripts/keys/prov8-shard-drift.cjs --gate` reports 6 current, 0 moved, 0 unmeasured over all four forks, and `audit-dataset-roster.cjs --gate` passes. `npm run regen` ran green end to end for the first time (exit 0 in 159s, ending in `emit-contract.cjs`), with the tree clean before and after it. Blocker 1 closed by the re-export chain 352f82c51 (the export itself) - ef3e3fd19 (the two population ratchets re-measured) - d81d8b7ae (the contract mirror) - 7f886ccf2 (the baseline stamp); blocker 2 by ed8047557 earlier. Read the title before believing this tick: it names main, and main still carries the September export, so main stays red on prov8 until this branch merges. The one thing still red on this branch is the formatting failure noted above, plus the two brainstorm Rust tests filed as unfiled-103.

`npm run baseline:write` run on a clean tree reached the write instead of stopping at the gate: the script's own prov8 step first reported 6 current, 0 moved, 0 unmeasured across all four forks, then `COH_WRITE_BASELINE=1 cargo test -p coh_math --test totals_baseline` wrote all four fixtures, and only `baseline/totals-brainstorm.json` moved - two lines, the recorded bundle stamp (73f51042c8178f35 -> 1b0bb1907de51c02) and its byte count (2,402,162 -> 2,407,054). The workaround this item was filed against (hand-running the cargo test with the env var set) was not needed. Landed on its own branch `prov8-beta-client-layout` off main as decided, in four commits: 352f82c51 the Brainstorm re-export from the 2026-11-03 beta bins, ef3e3fd19 the two population ratchets re-measured, d81d8b7ae the contract mirror, 7f886ccf2 this baseline. Two things this tick does NOT claim. body: Found 2026-11-11 while making the 2026-11-03 beta bin re-exportable. The parser now reads a fourth f4 between `arc` and the AreaFactor/PPMMod pair into `_field41a` and exports nothing from it (4bcb72236). Census: 0.0 on all 26,740 records of the beta bin, and 5.0 on one Archery power in the 2026-10-27 experimental bin - authored, not noise, and nothing in the export or the `.powers` defs names what it does. Layouts measured on this machine: live 2026-10-17 three words, closedbeta 2026-09-29 three words, experimental 2026-10-27 four, beta 2026-11-03 four. So live takes the change at its next patch, and when it does every manifest's parser fingerprint moves and all four forks re-export. `_detect_format` picks the width by scoring PPMMod == 1.0 and MaxBoosts == 6 alongside plausibility, because a short read in this block compensates for itself at the `has_field_45b` read and plausibility alone scores both widths 20/20 - that is why the misread survived as long as it did. says: The Nov 3 contract mirror breaks two coh_math tests: the brainstorm oracle's movementBuffValue on 13 sonic-melee and spines powers, and the sonic_attune test that asserts on a power the beta removed.
done_when: `cargo nextest run -p coh_math` is green with a ruling stated in the commit for both: the 13 either adjudicated field by field into the oracle or explained as a reader that should return nothing, and the Attune test either re-pointed at the target-side bonus or narrowed to the forks that still ship the caster-side one, with the removal said out loud either way.
body:
Found 2026-11-11 running `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` on the tree the re-export lands (394 of 396 green). Neither failure is a code change - no `.rs` file moved in the re-export chain - both are the new beta data arriving under assertions written against the September build.

1. `coh_math::oracle brainstorm`: `brainstorm/movementBuffValue: 13 of 3928 recorded powers disagree`, and every one reads `recorded: null` against `ours: []`. The 13 are Deafening Wave on Brute, Scrapper, Stalker and Tanker; Sandman's Whisper and Sonic Clap on Brute, Scrapper and Tanker; the Stalker's Assassin's Resonance; and the Stalker's Assassin's Impaler in the new Spines set. That is the Sonic Melee rework and the new set and nothing else, which is the same footprint the conditional-coverage re-measure found (unfiled-101's note and ef3e3fd19). The difference is presence-shaped rather than numeric - the TS record says the field is not there, this side says it is there and empty - so the first question is whether `movement_buff_value` should return nothing at all for a power whose only movement content sits inside a conditional group that is switched off, which is the shape the beta gave these powers. `COH_WRITE_ORACLE=1` exists and will make this green in one run; doing that without deciding the question above is how a frozen oracle stops meaning anything.

2. `coh_math::sonic_attune attune_switches_on_sonic_thrusts_bonus` panics at crates/coh_math/tests/sonic_attune.rs:92 with `Brainstorm: Attune on, Sonic Thrust deals no bonus`. Sonic Thrust is gone from the beta bin - its redirect file is one of the two the re-export deletes - and Attune no longer gates its caster at all: `sonicatuneself` fell 23 -> 8 and what ships instead is `sonicatunefoe` on Attune and `smattune` on the Stalker's Assassin's Resonance. So the mechanic this test pins does not exist on this fork any more. The fork still has a power named Sonic Thrust somewhere - `coh_math::foe_debuff_resistance sonic_thrusts_foe_debuff_resistance_is_a_debuff` passes on the same tree - so scoping the assertion to the forks that still carry the bonus is not enough on its own: somebody has to decide whether Brainstorm gets a test for the target-side bonus in its place or whether the coverage simply moves to the forks that kept the old one.

Found 2026-11-11 adjudicating the baseline write (7f886ccf2). `totals_baseline` reported the power database MOVED and the build corpus unchanged and then listed no differences at all - 37 builds, 37 identical answers - which is exactly what a blind grader looks like, so it was checked rather than enjoyed. The 37 builds in `fixtures/totals/brainstorm/synthetic.jsonl` wear Arachnos Soldier, Archery, Arsenal Assault, Arsenal Control, Assault Rifle, Atomic Manipulation, Battle Axe, Bio Armor, Cold Domination, Darkness Manipulation, Devices and their like. Against the 77 set directories the patch moved, the corpus overlaps on four, and those four's 13 changed files are: Sleet's and Freezing Rain's redirect lists dropping the pet `Avoid` targets that left the bin, Enforced Morale's magnitude flipping `Cur.kHitPoints` to the beta's lowercase spelling, and Arsenal Assault's Trip Mine gaining the AreaFactor override the parser used to mislabel. None of those reaches a number in CharacterStats or GlobalBonuses, which is the whole reason the diff is empty. Grepping the fixture for Sonic, Radiation, Spines and Energy Aura returns nothing: the sets the patch actually reworked are absent, so the one fixture that grades this fork's arithmetic watched nothing happen.

This is not a new axis - it is the gap `audit-atom-coverage.cjs --gate` already prints every run (143 builds, 169 distinct powers, 963 of 4,969 atom shapes covered) arriving with a cost attached. Whoever picks this up may decide the right move is feeding the atom-coverage corpus rather than growing the totals corpus, in which case close this item saying so.

evidence: Both failures adjudicated; no reader changed, because neither was one. (1) movementBuffValue: ruled the 13 records stale-by-data. Rewritten with COH_WRITE_ORACLE=1 in e16b42ca4; the diff is those 13 lines and nothing else (run twice, measured both times), all null -> []. Grounded in the frozen applier read at source, not inferred: movementBuffValue answers undefined ONLY when baseAtomsOfType(power,'Movement') is empty, keyedMovementEntries begins 'const out = []' and returns it so it cannot answer absent, isBagBase admits anything not gated and not archetype-forked, and the two copies of atom-query.ts are byte-identical across all three. Measured in the bundle: every one of the 13's movement atoms is gated=None, caster_archetypes=None, no DisplayOnly tag - so TS sees a non-empty base list and returns [] as well. The frozen fixture already answers [] for 96 records of this identical Resistance-aspect shape (Temporal Healing, Time Lord, Inexhaustible), and the 529 [] records still agree, which is what would have broken had the reader drifted instead of the data. (2) sonic_attune: 94e13862e grades the forks apart. Homecoming keeps the bonus assertion (SMAttune component resolving live, 108.44); Brainstorm gets sonic_thrust_keeps_no_attune_bonus_on_brainstorm, pinning a non-zero hit unmoved by Attune (31.69861 off, 31.69861 on) with no row naming the mark. Verified the new pin bites rather than grading a silence: pointed at Homecoming it fails. Gates on the final tree: cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast 397 run, 397 passed; npm run fmt:rust:check clean after 4a848f03c; audit-dataset-roster, audit-atom-coverage (963/4969, baseline held), audit-conditional-coverage, prov8-shard-drift (6 current, 0 moved) and export-integrity (58 ok, 0 failed) green; lint:js, lint:py, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean. NOT done: nothing pushed, the branch still has no upstream, and the owner has not seen any of it.

text: 2026-11-11, measured: two claims in this item's body are false, and the next reader should not reuse them. (1) The 13 are NOT movement content sitting inside a switched-off conditional group. Every one of those atoms reads gated=None on the current bundle - none is gated at all. The patch ADDED the rows: the September export holds no movement attrib whatsoever in these files, and the beta gave 11 of them RunningSpeed/FlyingSpeed/JumpingSpeed at aspect=Resistance on the always-on debuff group. The other two (Assassin's Resonance, Assassin's Impaler) hold effects:[] and take the same rows through their villain_pets redirect payloads, which the converter merges onto the parent. The question the body asked - whether a reader should answer absent when the only movement is behind a dead gate - never arises on this data. (2) Spines is not a new set: brute_melee/spines and mission_maker_attacks/spines are both in the September export at 4bcb72236. Third, softer: the body framed COH_WRITE_ORACLE as the tempting wrong answer. oracle.rs:690 sanctions it as the post-patch mechanism outright - 'the records are living, not frozen' - and asks only that the diff be read and each moved answer attributed to the patch first. What is forbidden is running it blind, not running it.

says: Brainstorm cannot assert its own Attune bonus: the rows that replaced Sonic Thrust's stay unresolved at every distance, so the fork has no number to pin.
body:
Found 2026-11-11 adjudicating unfiled-103, and it is the part of that ruling that did not get fixed. The Nov-3 patch took Sonic Thrust's caster-side Attune bonus out and put the mechanic on Attune itself, as kSonicAtuneFoe and kSonicAtune1Foe rows. Measured through recalculate on the current bundle, all of them arrive as unresolved - with distance unchosen, at 10 ft, and at 55 ft - and Attune offers no distance_bands at all, which target_distance.rs already asserts from its 20 ft reach. So sonic_thrust_keeps_no_attune_bonus_on_brainstorm can only pin the removal structurally. Homecoming's foe-mark path is graded by a value (the SMAttune component, 108.44, resolving live because the projection infers the mark from the caster's own running Attune); Brainstorm's is graded by the absence of rows, which is the weaker claim and will not notice a wrong magnitude.

What has to change is one of two things, and nobody has established which. Either the projection gains a way to be told what modes the target carries, rather than only inferring them from the caster, or the tier-1 mark has to reach the build by the route the beta now uses - the SMAttune group is an Execute_Power of Redirects.Sonic_Melee.Attune, and nothing in this build grants kSonicAtune1Foe, which is why that half stays unsettled. Note the second is a question about the engine, not this test: if the redirect's payload never reaches the projection, a player on Brainstorm cannot see their own Attune bonus either.

Same blind spot as unfiled-104, one level up: the totals corpus wears none of the sets this patch reworked, and the one test that does reach them asserts shape rather than value.

Found 2026-11-11 by running the two def gates this time with COH_RAW_DEFS pointed at the real defs, which the last session could not do: it resolved them to /home/jiiwii/Github/coh-sidekick/coh-sidekick-refdata/raw defs, a path the workspace move deleted, while the defs live at /home/jiiwii/Github/Sidekick Archive/coh-sidekick-refdata/raw defs. They print a skip rather than going quiet, so nothing looked wrong - but on any machine holding the defs this branch is red and main is not. Measured, not inferred: at 4bcb72236 in a throwaway worktree the gate reports OK, 0 dropped, exit 0; on this tree it reports FAIL with 20, exit 1. CI runs neither gate - ci.yml:185 mentions them only inside a Python-version note - so this blocks no merge.

None of the 20 is a parser drop, which is the thing worth recording. Every one is Brute/Scrapper/Stalker/Tanker Spines and Scrapper Quills, and every one says the def deals Toxic_Dmg while the power's own effect tree no longer does. Barb_Swipe is the shape: September held Toxic_Dmg scale=0.1 inline under tags=[SpinePoison]; the beta's same group now holds a RunningSpeed/FlyingSpeed/JumpingSpeed and RechargeTime Melee_Slow and a child Execute_Power of Redirects.Spines.SpinePoison, and that payload carries the Toxic_Dmg as an Expression at scale=0.025 over 9.1 s with a PoisonedStatus Set_Mode beside it. Checked the payload resolves for all 20, not the one - 20/20 carry Toxic_Dmg through their Execute_Power. tools/defdiff.py:export_templates walks effects and child_effects only, so a mechanic that leaves the tree via Execute_Power reads as missing. This is the same footprint as unfiled-103's sonic_attune failure: the Nov-3 patch relocated mechanics behind Execute_Power, and every reader that looks only inside the power sees a removal. Two gates and one test have now tripped on it in one day, which is the argument for fixing the reader rather than the list twice more.

UNMEASURED, and deliberately not asserted here: whether that poison reaches a player at all. The Brainstorm bundle carries 4,892 Toxic tokens and 154 SpinePoison ones but no Toxic_Dmg string - the damage type travels as a subType, so that count says nothing either way - and nothing in the bundle looks like a SpinePoison power record. If the executed payload never reaches the projection, Brainstorm players cannot see their own poison ticks, which is an engine question, not an audit one, and the same unknown unfiled-105 records for Attune. Answer that before treating the allowlist as the whole fix.

body: Measured 2026-11-11 through coh_math::recalculate on the Nov-3 bundle (scratch test, deleted). The poison does reach the projection: Barb_Swipe, Lunge and Impale on Brainstorm brute/spines and scrapper/spines each carry one UnresolvedDamage row, Toxic, empty gate, if_it_lands None, reason 'magnitude expression [Temporary_Powers.Temporary_Powers.Poison target.ownPowerNum? .9 * 1 + @StdResult *] depends on target.ownPowerNum?, which this context does not model'. That is by design: expr.rs:897 leaves target.ownPowerNum? unanswered because the target is a per-cast fact. Redirects.Spines.SpinePoison deals 0.025 Melee_Damage Toxic over 9.1 s, times (1 + 0.9 x the Poison stacks the target already holds), and grants one more stack each hit. Three things a player sees: (1) the line prints the raw token list; (2) tags come through empty, so the SpinePoison name is lost (it sits on the redirect's outer group, the damage on an inner one); (3) the hit total drops the poison entirely - Brute Impale 175.18 on Homecoming vs 75.08 on Brainstorm, Barb_Swipe 44.89 vs 35.04. The first application (0 stacks) has a knowable floor of 1 x StdResult, so a floor value is possible. Same family as unfiled-105: the projection cannot be told the target's state.

Unset is 0, a fresh target, so every hit has a number from the start. Only the per-power projection answers it; the totals pass leaves it Indeterminate so no total can move. Corpus today: Brainstorm Temporary_Powers.Poison (Spines, cap 10) and Rebirth Rage_Exposure (Clockwork critter powers only, so no player sees it). Still open, not fixed by this: the Brainstorm Toxic row carries no SpinePoison name, because the tag sits on the redirect's outer group and the damage on an inner one.

title: Build a character from scratch on a phone
thesis: On a phone (the below-900px layout), a user can take an empty build to a fully slotted one through the Build tab alone: choose a power for every pick level, place every extra slot, and fill every slot through the existing enhancement picker, while four key numbers stay on screen and show what a choice would change before it is committed; everything else the app shows sits behind the Stats and More tabs.
body:
Asked for 2026-11-11, owner: continue the mobile UI overhaul, following docs/mockups/phone-build-flow.html (committed cffab299c). Owner learned the same day that phone users build whole characters from scratch on the phone, so the phone is a builder, not a viewer.

Decided 2026-11-11, owner (each was the recommended option):
- The three-job flow replaces the phone's main screen. Today's stacked panels move behind the Stats and More tabs.
- The bottom bar becomes Build / Stats / More. Dashboard's contents go to Stats; Options, Incarnate and the file/tools/help menus go to More.
- The four numbers pinned at the top default per archetype and the user can swap any of them.
- Filling slots reuses the existing enhancement picker; the mockup's own power sheet is not built.
- Moving a chosen power to another level by hold-and-drop is not in the first version.

Agent's rules, not objected to yet:
- 'Phone' means the existing below-900px stacked layout. Nothing changes at 900px and up.
- The top numbers are rows of the stat registry (panels/stat_registry.rs), so their labels, units and colours come from the same place the desktop's totals do. The per-archetype defaults live in one authored table, not in conditionals.
- Every edit goes through BuildSession::commit, so undo, redo, saving and cloud sync work as they do on desktop.
- Which powers a level may take comes from pick_gate and the Available panel's existing rules, never re-derived for the phone.

Preconditions, checked 2026-11-11:
- panels/powers.rs add_power(state, powerset_id, internal_name, level, role) adds a power at a given pick level.
- panels/powers.rs pick_gate reads a power's prerequisites against the build; the Available panel already lists eligible powers per set.
- panels/powers.rs add_slot_to_power and remove_slot_from_power exist.
- coh_math::recalculate(&CharacterState, &PowerDatabase) takes any state, so a not-yet-committed build can be totalled for a preview.
- tracked_stats.rs keeps a user's chosen stat rows by StatDef id; mobile_order.rs keeps the phone's panel order.
- mobile_nav.rs holds today's five-tab bar and its sheets; build_bar.rs already opens Build Identity from the top on phones (e6da75a4d).
- qa-check runs Pixel 7 (Chromium) and iPhone 13 (WebKit, in a container) profiles.

Out of scope:
- The desktop layout, and touch screens 900px wide or more: they keep the grid.
- Moving a chosen power by hold-and-drop: owner deferred it; tap to change or remove, then re-pick.
- A phone-only enhancement sheet: owner chose the existing picker.
- Redesigning the incarnate picker, attack chain, set bonus finder, compare or other tools: they are reached from More as they are.
- Syncing the top-number choice across devices: that belongs to layout-sync.
- Choosing the level each slot is added at on phones: the slot gets the level the existing add_slot_to_power gives it.

says: Four key numbers sit under the build bar on phones, read from the stat registry. Each archetype has a default four in one authored table; the user can swap any of them from the Stats tab; tapping one opens Stats.
done_when: A test checks every archetype in all four datasets has four defaults, each a real stat registry id. On a phone, charnel.txt shows the Tanker's four with the same values as the desktop's totals; swapping one survives a reload.

says: The Build tab shows a three-way switch (Powers, Slots, Enhance) with a count on each, and the Powers job lists every pick level in order: the chosen power and its slot count, or 'Choose a power' with the first empty one marked Next, plus a bottom button for the next empty level.
done_when: On a phone, an empty Tanker shows 24 levels with level 1 marked Next; charnel.txt shows 24 of 24 and every power at the level the desktop's By Level view gives it.

says: Tapping a level opens a sheet listing the powers that level can take, grouped primary, secondary, pools and epic, with powers it cannot take shown greyed with the reason (level, already taken, pool limit, prerequisite). Taking one commits it at that level and moves the sheet to the next empty level. Tapping a chosen power offers change or remove.

done_when: On a phone, an empty-slotted build places all extra slots through the plus buttons and the count reaches 0 left; the slot totals match the desktop's slot counter; undo removes the last slot.

says: The Enhance job lists each chosen power with its slots drawn as small enhancement icons and how many are empty. Tapping one opens the existing enhancement picker on that power's first empty slot; a bottom button opens the next power with empty slots.
done_when: On Pixel 7 and iPhone 13, a fully slotted but unenhanced build is filled through the Enhance list and the picker alone, including a set, a generic IO and a special; the list's icons match what the picker committed.

says: While a choice is pending, the four key numbers show how each would change if it were committed: a power under the finger in the pick sheet, or the marked and held pieces in the enhancement picker. The change shown equals what the numbers become once it is committed.
done_when: A test commits a pending choice on fixture builds and checks the numbers after equal the preview. On a phone, holding a set piece in the picker shows a change on Def or Res for charnel.txt, and committing it lands on that value.

done_when: On a phone with empty storage: after the welcome, the screen offers starting a build; finishing Build Identity shows the Powers job with level 1 marked Next and its sheet one tap away.

says: The owner builds a character from scratch on a physical phone using only the Build tab, and finds nothing they had to reach for the old stacked layout to do.
done_when: The owner reports building a full character on their own phone and lists anything that was missing or awkward; each such thing is opened as a finding.

title: Slots on the power cards
thesis: On a phone, the Build tab is one list: each chosen power card shows its slots as circles (grey when empty, filled in the in-game colour of the set type or enhancement type when slotted), and a Slots button on the card unfolds the slots beneath it, where each slot opens the enhancement picker and slots can be added and removed, so the separate Slots and Enhance passes are no longer needed.
body:
Asked for 2026-11-12, owner: streamline the phone build flow by giving each power card a Slots button that unfolds its slots beneath the card; folded, empty slots are grey circles and slotted ones colour-coded filled circles.

Decided 2026-11-12, owner:
- One list for everything: the Powers list carries the circles and the Slots button; the Slots and Enhance passes and the three-way switch go away.
- The unfolded area both fills (a slot opens the existing enhancement picker) and adds/removes slots.
- Colours follow the game: a set piece takes its set type colour (all damage set types are red, Holds orange, Defense purple and so on); a single-stat enhancement takes its stat colour. The colours are read off the game art in crates/app/assets/img/Enhancements/Components/POGS.

Agent decisions 2026-11-12: set types with no single colour (archetype sets, Universal sets) take the piece first stat; a special (Hamidon, Titan, Hydra, D-Sync) takes its first stat. One card unfolds at a time.

Preconditions, checked 2026-11-12: every set type across the four datasets is listed (46-49 per dataset); set-piece aspects and common IO stats use one small vocabulary (about 30 names); the POGS folder has 32 images, one per enhancement stat; slot room, add and remove come from panels/powers.rs slot_room, add_slot_to_power and remove_slot_from_power.

Out of scope:
- The desktop. Its slots already show the enhancement art.
- Moving slots between powers by drag: not asked for.
- Colouring the picker or tooltips: the circles are the only new colour use.

says: A rule gives each slotted enhancement one in-game colour: its set type for a set piece, its stat for any other, falling back to the first stat where the set type has none.
Each chosen power card in the phone Powers list shows a circle per slot: grey when empty, filled in its colour when slotted.
done_when: On a phone, charnel.txt shows each power card with one circle per slot; Dark Embrace (Defense sets) reads purple, a Damage set piece reads red, and an emptied slot reads grey.

says: A Slots button on each card unfolds its slots beneath it: each slot shows its enhancement and opens the picker on that slot, and a minus and plus button with the slots left add and remove slots. One card is unfolded at a time.
done_when: On a phone, tapping Slots on a card unfolds it and folds any other; tapping a slot opens the picker on that slot and a filled piece shows on return; plus and minus change the count and the slots-left figure, and stop at the same limits as the desktop.

says: The inherent powers that take enhancements (Health, Stamina, Sprint and the like) appear at the foot of the list with the same circles and Slots button.
done_when: On a phone, charnel.txt lists Health, Stamina and its other slotted inherents after the last pick level, and one can be unfolded and filled like a pick.

says: The Powers, Slots and Enhance switch is gone; the list header says how many picks, slots and filled slots the build has, and the foot button leads to the next empty level, then the next power with an empty slot.
done_when: On a phone, the switch is not drawn, the header counts match the desktop counters, and on a fully picked build the foot button opens the picker on the first empty slot.

says: The owner slots and fills a build on a physical phone using only the cards.
done_when: The owner places and fills slots on their own phone through the unfolding cards and reports nothing they had to look for elsewhere.

evidence: slot_colour.rs: every_set_piece_has_a_colour and every_single_stat_and_special_has_a_colour load all four bundles and pass; breaking the Recharge mapping made both fail, naming Homecoming common IO Recharge and an ATO piece. 213/213 app tests.

Pixel 7 and iPhone 13 (WebKit), charnel.txt: Smite six red (#f00000), Health three green, Stamina dark blue, Taunt black ringed; a re-added empty slot draws a hollow ring. Dark Embrace reads cyan, not purple as done_when guessed: it is a Resist Damage power, so cyan is right.
