title: Delete your own account
thesis: A signed-in person can delete their own Sidekick account from the account menu, and afterwards the server holds nothing tied to it: no sign-in record, profile, favourites, saved layout, published builds or build preview images.
body:
Player report, 2026-11-13, from the in-app bug form (account "ennuisance"): there is no way to
delete an account. Checked the same day: the app's account code can only sign in and out, and the
only delete on the server is `delete-build`.

Decision, 2026-11-13, user-chosen: **a deleted account's published builds are deleted with it.**
Rejected: keeping them with no owner (favourites keep working, but nobody but the owner of the
project could ever edit or remove them, and they still carry the author's name).

The server is the Supabase project both apps use (`utnqoueoiixygoqerfiw`). Its schema and edge
functions live in `~/Github/coh-sidekick/coh-sidekick-beta/supabase/`, which is linked to that
project. The live database and the dashboard are changed only with the owner's go-ahead
(account-deletion-1).

## Preconditions

Checked 2026-11-13:

- Live foreign keys to `auth.users` (read-only query): `profiles`, `favorites` and `user_layouts`
  are `ON DELETE CASCADE`; `shared_builds_user_id_fkey` is NO ACTION, so a user who owns any build
  cannot be deleted today, from the dashboard or anywhere else. Matches `schema.sql:26`.
- `favorites.build_id` cascades from `shared_builds`, so deleting a build already clears other
  people's favourites of it.
- Each build's preview image is at a fixed path in the public `build-previews` bucket
  (`previewObjectPath(id)`); `delete-build` already removes it the same way.
- The Supabase CLI here is logged in and reaches the project (`supabase functions list`).
- The project allows email sign-in, so a throwaway test account can be made with the admin API
  for the in-app check, rather than borrowing a real Discord account.
- The beta repo's tree is clean. This repo has someone's unrelated uncommitted edits
  (`ed_view.rs`, `ed_breakdown.rs`, `app.css`); leave them alone.

## Out of scope

- **A button in the beta app.** The server function serves both apps; the beta's UI can call it later.
- **Builds shared anonymously before signing in.** They answer to a browser token, not an account, and
  were never the account's.
- **An undo or grace period.** A deleted account is gone; the confirmation says so instead.
- **Exporting your data first.** Builds can already be saved as files one by one.
- **Deleting other people's accounts.** That stays a dashboard job for the owner, which the cascade
  change also makes possible.

body: Found 2026-11-13 during the account-deletion check. `layout_sync::tick` reads the user id, then waits on `Account::prepared`, which waits for the lock that `sign_out` and `delete_account` hold across their server call. When it gets the lock the session is gone, so `prepared` hands back the signed-out client and `reconcile` fetches `user_layouts` with the anon key. Harmless (a read, refused; the next tick sees no user), but it is a console error. Likely fix: after `prepared`, give up the tick if the user signal no longer names the same id.

title: A henchman's buff on its Mastermind reaches the totals
thesis: On every fork, a Mastermind holding Protector Bots or Summon Demons can switch on that henchman's buff, and the totals then carry Force Shield's defense once (raised by Defense slotting in Protector Bots) or both Ember Shields' resistance (flat, or raised by Resistance slotting in Summon Demons once Enchant Demon is in the build).
body:
Player request, 2026-11-13, from the in-app feature form (account "greenandpurple", a Robotics/Traps Mastermind): "Robots and Demon second tier pets have auras that should be display-able on your defense/resist total respectively."

## What the data says (measured 2026-11-13, pipeline/<fork>/pet-entities.json)

Across all four forks, exactly two Mastermind henchmen carry a buff whose recipients include their owner. No other henchman does (heals aside).

- **Protector Bot** (`Protector_Bots`): `Force_Shield`, a Click on `MyOwner` (Homecoming, Brainstorm) or `Friend` (Rebirth, Thunderspy), +Defense 1.3 x `Ranged_Buff_Def` to every position and six types, 240 s, recharge 8 s. The export says `caster_stack: Collective`, `stack: Replace`: two bots' shields on one owner are ONE shield, so it is counted once. `boosts_allowed` takes Buff_Defense and the summon is `copyBoosts`, so the summon power's Defense slotting raises it. Equip Robot and Upgrade Robot add nothing that reaches the owner.
- **Ember Demon** (`Summon_Demons`): two Autos, `Shield_of_Hellfire` (Friend, 0.5/0.666/0.333 x `Ranged_Res_Dmg`) and `Ember_Shield_Owner` (MyOwner, 1.0/1.333/0.666), both to Smashing, Lethal, Toxic, Fire, Cold. The owner gets both: the owner power's help text says "an additional damage resistance ... to its owner", and they are separate powers so their stacking never meets. `Shield_of_Hellfire` also has a demon-only second copy (`target.VillainName` gate); the converter already leaves it out of `effects`. Both base powers are IgnoreStrength. `Enchant_Demon` REVOKES both and grants `Ember_Demon_2` versions without IgnoreStrength and with Res_Damage allowed, so only after that upgrade does Resistance slotting raise them.

## Decisions

Decided 2026-11-13, agent: these ride the existing opt-in buff-pet switch (`buff_pets.rs`), off by default, exactly as Force Field Generator does. The request says "display-able", and a henchman can die or be dismissed, so a switch is the honest shape.

Decided 2026-11-13, agent: the admission rule is the game's own class taxonomy, the same one `fights_as_a_companion` already uses: a commandable entity whose class names `henchman`. Commandability alone would also admit Lore and Fate incarnate pets, which are out (below).

Decided 2026-11-13, agent: the upgrade swap is read from the `upgradeTiers` block the pet converter already emits (`grantedBy`, `revokes`, `abilities`), which reaches the shipped bundle and which no Rust code reads yet. Nothing names Enchant Demon in code.

## Preconditions

Checked 2026-11-13:

- The census above holds on all four forks' generated pet-entities.
- `upgradeTiers` is in `contract/homecoming/bundle.json.gz`.
- The fold already leaves an `ignoreStrength` row unenhanced (`enh_multiplier`), so the base Ember Shields stay flat with no new code.
- `summoned_entity_chain` skips every commandable entity; damage, procs and the display bag read through it, so the admission has to be a separate walk or they would start folding henchman attacks.

## Out of scope

- Lore and Fate incarnate pets (Mind Link, Shield Generator, Field Projector and the rest): also commandable and also buff their owner, but they are not what was asked and they have their own uptime questions.
- Heals a henchman casts on its owner (Repair, Abyssal Mending): a heal is not a total.
- Buffs a henchman puts on other henchmen: those are the pets' own numbers, not the Mastermind's.
- Henchman level offset: tables are read at the character's level, as the existing fold does. If the two tables move between the henchman's level and the Mastermind's this would be a separate, measured finding.
